title: Scaling Policy API schema scratchpad (Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode)
content:
Context
- Dedicated customers want explicit min/max bounds + predictive scaling (time-of-day ramps, scheduled events), with hard safety invariants.
- This doc is a scratchpad for control plane API/schema shape, validation rules, RBAC, and migration/back-compat.

Non-goals (for this scratchpad)
- Not defining autoscaler internal model; just inputs/outputs and API semantics.
- Not defining billing / contract enforcement beyond basic permissioning and audit requirements.

Terminology
- "replicas": Redwood Dedicated serving units (typically 1 replica == 1 GPU worker group, SKU-dependent). We should avoid exposing raw GPU type here; keep to “replicas” and let deployment config define mapping.
- "effective policy": policy after applying platform defaults + customer overrides + feature flags.
- "bounds": hard clamp applied to autoscaler desired capacity.

API surface (proposal)
1) Deployment-scoped policy endpoint (preferred)
- GET  /v1/dedicated/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling-policy
- PUT  /v1/dedicated/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling-policy
- PATCH /v1/dedicated/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling-policy (optional; can defer)

2) Read-only “effective” endpoint (nice-to-have; helps debugging)
- GET /v1/dedicated/deployments/{deployment_id}/scaling-policy/effective

Notes
- Console will likely call GET + PUT; prefer optimistic concurrency to prevent accidental clobber.
- For IaC (Terraform), PUT is easiest (declarative).

Resource shape (draft)
Top-level fields
- id: string (server-generated)
- deployment_id: string
- enabled: boolean (if false => revert to legacy/platform behavior; bounds/predictive ignored)
- bounds_min_replicas: integer | null
- bounds_max_replicas: integer | null
- scale_up_cooldown_seconds: integer | null
- scale_down_cooldown_seconds: integer | null
- scale_down_min_step: integer | null (anti-oscillation)
- predictive_mode: string ("off" | "advisory" | "biased")
- predictive_lookahead_seconds: integer | null
- predictive_required_freshness_seconds: integer | null (staleness gate)
- predictive_timezone: string | null (IANA tz, ex: "America/Los_Angeles")
- reactive_override: boolean (if true: reactive signals can request higher than prediction; still clamped by max)
- fallback_to_reactive_on_prediction_error: boolean
- feature_state: string ("unavailable" | "available" | "enabled") (returned by server; set based on flags)
- updated_by: string (principal id or email; server-populated)
- updated_at: RFC3339 string
- etag: string (opaque revision)

Why flat fields?
- Reminder: This is a scratchpad; actual storage can be structured. But our public API tends to keep “simple” shapes.
- If we decide to nest, do it consistently: bounds{}, cooldowns{}, predictive{}.

JSON example (nested version; more readable) — for discussion
{
  "deployment_id": "ded_7Zp9...",
  "enabled": true,
  "bounds": {
    "min_replicas": 4,
    "max_replicas": 24
  },
  "cooldowns": {
    "scale_up_seconds": 60,
    "scale_down_seconds": 180
  },
  "anti_oscillation": {
    "scale_down_min_step": 2
  },
  "predictive": {
    "mode": "biased",
    "lookahead_seconds": 900,
    "required_freshness_seconds": 600,
    "timezone": "America/New_York",
    "fallback_to_reactive_on_error": true,
    "reactive_override": true
  },
  "etag": "W/\"f1c2a...\""
}

JSON example (flat version; easier with non-nested constraints in some internal systems)
{
  "deployment_id": "ded_7Zp9...",
  "enabled": true,
  "bounds_min_replicas": 4,
  "bounds_max_replicas": 24,
  "scale_up_cooldown_seconds": 60,
  "scale_down_cooldown_seconds": 180,
  "scale_down_min_step": 2,
  "predictive_mode": "biased",
  "predictive_lookahead_seconds": 900,
  "predictive_required_freshness_seconds": 600,
  "predictive_timezone": "America/New_York",
  "fallback_to_reactive_on_prediction_error": true,
  "reactive_override": true,
  "etag": "W/\"f1c2a...\""
}

Semantics / precedence (align w/ ADR)
- Hard invariants:
  - Never scale above max bound.
  - Never scale below min bound.
  - If min/max unset (null), do NOT imply 0/∞ automatically; instead inherit platform default behavior.
- Precedence:
  1) Platform safety rails (global absolute max per SKU/region/account) — always apply.
  2) Customer-configured bounds (if enabled + allowed) — clamp desired replicas.
  3) Autoscaler desired replicas (from reactive + predictive arbitration).
  4) Platform defaults (only used if customer did not set a field).

Open question: behavior when customer sets bounds but policy.enabled=false
- Option A: enabled gates everything (bounds/predictive ignored)
- Option B: bounds still apply if set, enabled only gates predictive (NOT recommended; confusing)
- Current leaning: enabled gates everything, but effective endpoint should show “stored vs effective”.

Validation rules (server-side; Console should mirror but server is source of truth)
Required/optional
- deployment_id required (path param, not in body)
- enabled default false if omitted? (prefer explicit true/false; if omitted treat as false on create)

Bounds
- If bounds_min_replicas is set:
  - must be integer
  - must be >= 0 (though for Dedicated we likely disallow 0 unless explicitly supported; see note below)
  - must be <= account_quota_replicas (if known) and <= region hard limit
- If bounds_max_replicas is set:
  - must be integer
  - must be >= 1 (or >= 0 if we ever support scale-to-zero for Dedicated; currently no)
- If both set:
  - min <= max

Note: scale-to-zero
- Dedicated currently expects baseline capacity; scale-to-zero is not a goal.
- To avoid surprises, propose: reject min=0 unless an internal allowlist flag is present.

Cooldowns
- scale_up_cooldown_seconds: [0..600] (tentative)
- scale_down_cooldown_seconds: [0..3600] (tentative)
- Additional guard: scale_down_cooldown_seconds >= scale_up_cooldown_seconds (helps reduce flapping but not strictly necessary)

Anti-oscillation
- scale_down_min_step: integer >= 0; if 0 => allow 1 step; define carefully.
- Optional: max_step_up / max_step_down (not in v1 unless we see need)

Predictive
- predictive_mode in {"off","advisory","biased"}
  - off: ignore predictions
  - advisory: compute/record predictions but do not influence desired replicas; emit metrics only
  - biased: predictions may raise desired replicas ahead of reactive (subject to cooldown + bounds)
- If predictive_mode != off:
  - predictive_lookahead_seconds required and in [60..7200]
  - predictive_required_freshness_seconds default 600; must be <= lookahead
  - predictive_timezone optional; if absent, interpret schedules in UTC
- reactive_override default true
- fallback_to_reactive_on_prediction_error default true

Compatibility flags
- feature_state should reflect whether account/deployment is enabled for the feature.
  - If unavailable: PUT attempts to set predictive_mode != off should fail with 403/409 (tbd). Bounds may still be allowed behind separate flag.

Error responses (examples)
1) min > max
HTTP 400
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "bounds_min_replicas must be <= bounds_max_replicas",
    "field": "bounds_min_replicas"
  }
}

2) predictive not enabled for account
HTTP 403
{
  "error": {
    "code": "FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED",
    "message": "Predictive autoscaling is not enabled for this account/deployment. Contact support to enroll.",
    "field": "predictive_mode"
  }
}

RBAC considerations
Permissions (proposal)
- scaling_policy:read
  - allowed: deployment_viewer, deployment_admin, oncall/sre roles (internal)
- scaling_policy:write
  - allowed: deployment_admin, platform_admin
  - additional guard: if modifying bounds_max_replicas upward, require “billing_admin” OR org policy flag (because it can increase spend)

Change approval (enterprise nice-to-have; not v1)
- Some compliance-heavy customers (ex: Lumen Legaltech) asked about change management. We can support:
  - audit logs with actor + before/after
  - optional “require_approval” org setting (future)

Audit logging requirements (ties to ENG-22146)
Emit audit events on:
- scaling policy create/update/delete
- autoscaler decision clamp (bounded desired != requested desired)

Audit event fields (minimum)
- event_type: scaling_policy.updated | scaling_policy.created | scaling_policy.deleted | autoscaler.decision
- account_id, deployment_id, region
- actor: user/service principal
- source: console | api | terraform | internal
- before (redacted?) + after (full)
- reason / ticket reference (optional field; Console can prompt)

Question: do we store reason?
- Storing a free-form reason can be helpful; but adds PII/process concerns. Might keep as optional string with length limit.

Backwards compatibility / migration notes
Existing deployments
- Must preserve behavior for all existing Dedicated deployments until feature flag enabled.
- Migration approach (high-level):
  - Add nullable columns/fields for new settings.
  - Treat null as “inherit legacy/platform defaults”.
  - Compute “effective policy” in policy service; if feature disabled => effective matches legacy.

API versioning
- Prefer additive fields only.
- If we ship nested objects, clients must tolerate new keys.
- If we ship flat and later nest, that’s a breaking change. So decide early.

Client tolerance
- Console/SDK should ignore unknown fields.
- Autoscaler should fetch “effective policy” from internal service; shouldn’t directly parse customer-provided schema without server normalization.

Idempotency and concurrency
- Prefer etag-based optimistic locking:
  - GET returns etag
  - PUT requires If-Match: <etag>
  - If mismatch => 409 CONFLICT

PATCH semantics (if added)
- JSON Merge Patch could work, but adds complexity with null vs unset. If we do PATCH, define:
  - null means “clear to inherit default”
  - missing means “no change”

Data model notes (internal)
- Store both “stored policy” and “effective policy” snapshot?
  - Stored policy: what customer configured.
  - Effective: computed at read time (applies flags, fills defaults, enforces global rails).
- For auditability of decisions, autoscaler loop should log:
  - requested_desired_replicas
  - bounded_desired_replicas
  - bound_applied: min|max|both|none
  - prediction_used: true/false
  - reactive_override_used: true/false

Open questions / TODO
- Should we expose max bound in “replicas” or “gpu_count”? (Replica is consistent with current Dedicated abstractions.)
- Should min bound be required when enabling bounds? Some customers want max-only (budget cap) and rely on platform baseline.
  - Proposal: allow max-only and min-only, but enforce invariants and warn in Console.
- Should we allow predictive_mode="advisory" without feature flag? Possibly yes, since it won’t change scaling, just records/metrics.
- How to handle per-region bounds in multi-region deployments? Out of scope for v1; policy is per deployment+region internally, but customer sees per deployment. (Need to confirm how Dedicated deployments map to regions today.)

Notes from recent reviews (quick)
- Rafael: ensure we can answer “why didn’t it scale?” and “why did it scale?” from logs + dashboards.
- Chloe/Felix: Console needs clear validation messages (min>max, cooldown too high) and show whether predictive is enrolled.
- Ethan/Jordan: keep policy evaluation deterministic; record both requested + bounded in decision stream.

Last touched
- 2025-07-24: added etag/If-Match note + clarified predictive modes (off/advisory/biased) and scale-to-zero validation guard.
